questions.stem: The factorization of 15x²y as a product of its factors is:
questions.explanation: 15x²y = (5x)(3xy). This is direct product factorization; 5x × 3xy = 15x²y.

questions.stem: The factorization of a⁴ + a²b² + b⁴ is:
questions.explanation: a⁴ + a²b² + b⁴: add and subtract a²b² to form (a² + b²)² − (ab)² = (a² + b² + ab)(a² + b² − ab).

questions.stem: a⁴ + 64b⁴ factorizes as:
questions.explanation: a⁴ + 64b⁴ = (a² + 8b²)² − (4ab)² = (a² + 8b² + 4ab)(a² + 8b² − 4ab).

questions.stem: Which of the following is the factored form of x⁴ + 4m⁴?
questions.explanation: x⁴ + 4m⁴ = (x² + 2m²)² − (2xm)² = (x² + 2m² + 2xm)(x² + 2m² − 2xm).

questions.stem: The factored form of y² − 7y + 12 is:
questions.explanation: y² − 7y + 12: factors of 12 with sum −7 are −3 and −4 → (y − 3)(y − 4).

questions.stem: The factored form of m² − 2m − 15 is:
questions.explanation: m² − 2m − 15: factors of −15 with sum −2 are −5 and +3 → (m − 5)(m + 3).

questions.stem: The factored form of 3x² + 22x − 16 is:
questions.explanation: 3x² + 22x − 16: product = −48; pair with sum 22 is 24, −2 → 3x² + 24x − 2x − 16 = (x + 8)(3x − 2).

questions.stem: The factored form of x² + x − 2 is:
questions.explanation: x² + x − 2: factors of −2 with sum +1 are +2 and −1 → (x + 2)(x − 1).

questions.stem: When factorizing (x² + 3x − 4)(x² + 3x + 5) + 8, substituting a = x² + 3x gives:
questions.explanation: Substituting a = x² + 3x, the expression becomes (a − 4)(a + 5) + 8.

questions.stem: The factored form of (x² + 3x − 4)(x² + 3x + 5) + 8 is:
questions.explanation: (a − 4)(a + 5) + 8 = a² + a − 12 = (a + 4)(a − 3); replacing a gives (x² + 3x + 4)(x² + 3x − 3).

questions.stem: The identity a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ equals:
questions.explanation: Binomial cube identity: a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ = (a + b)³.

questions.stem: The factored form of x³ + 27y³ is:
questions.explanation: x³ + 27y³ = x³ + (3y)³ = (x + 3y)(x² − 3xy + 9y²).

The HCF of 18ab³c, 30a²b⁴c³, and 24b²c⁵ is:
questions.explanation: HCF of coefficients 18, 30, 24 is 6; least power of b is b², least power of c is c → HCF = 6b²c.

questions.stem: The HCF of two or more polynomials is the polynomial that:
options: divides each of them exactly and is of highest degree
is divisible by each of them
is the product of all their factors
has the lowest degree among all factors
questions.explanation: The HCF of polynomials divides each of them exactly and is of the highest possible degree.

questions.stem: The HCF of x² − 49 and x² − 4x − 21 is:
questions.explanation: x² − 49 = (x−7)(x+7); x² − 4x − 21 = (x−7)(x+3). The common factor is x − 7.

questions.stem: When finding the HCF of monomials, the HCF of the variable part is determined by taking:
options: the highest power of each variable
the lowest power of each common variable
questions.explanation: For monomials, variable HCF = lowest power of each common variable appearing in all terms.

questions.stem: The LCM of two polynomials P and Q with HCF H is given by:
questions.explanation: LCM = (P × Q) ÷ HCF. This is the standard formula relating LCM, HCF and the two polynomials.

questions.stem: The product of two polynomials P and Q equals:
questions.explanation: P × Q = HCF × LCM is the fundamental theorem for any two polynomials.

questions.stem: If HCF of two polynomials is x − 7 and their LCM is x³ − 10x² + 11x + 70, their product is:
questions.explanation: Product = HCF × LCM = (x − 7)(x³ − 10x² + 11x + 70).

questions.stem: An algebraic fraction P/Q is defined when:
options: P and Q are polynomials and Q ≠ 0
P and Q are integers only
questions.explanation: An algebraic fraction P/Q requires P and Q to be polynomials with Q ≠ 0.

questions.stem: To add algebraic fractions with different denominators, we first find their:
questions.explanation: A common denominator (LCM of denominators) is required before adding algebraic fractions.

To divide one algebraic fraction by another, we multiply the first fraction by:
options: the reciprocal of the second fraction
questions.explanation: (P/Q) ÷ (R/S) = (P/Q) × (S/R): multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor fraction.

questions.stem: The square root of a perfect square polynomial can be found by:
questions.explanation: Square roots of algebraic expressions are found by factorization method or division method.

questions.stem: The square root of 9x² − 42xy + 49y² is:
questions.explanation: 9x² − 42xy + 49y² = (3x − 7y)² → square root = ±(3x − 7y).

questions.stem: The expression x⁴ − 6x³ + 17x² − 24x + 16 has the square root:
questions.explanation: x⁴ − 6x³ + 17x² − 24x + 16 = (x² − 3x + 4)² → square root = ±(x² − 3x + 4).
